title: Countable successor closure and exhaustion by coordinate stages
statement: Let $J$ be a set, $C\subseteq J$ an at most countable subset, and $(F_j)_{j\in J}$ a family of at most countable subsets of $J$. Define $A_0=C$, $A_{k+1}=A_k\cup\bigcup_{j\in A_k}F_j$ for $k\in\mathbf N$, and $D=\bigcup_{k\in\mathbf N}A_k$. Then the sequence $(A_k)$ is increasing, every $A_k$ and $D$ are at most countable, $C\subseteq D$, and $F_j\subseteq D$ for every $j\in D$. Every finite subset $E\subseteq D$ is contained in some $A_k$, including $E=\varnothing$. For any commutative ring $R$ and any family $(N_j)_{j\in J}$ of $R$-modules, put $M=\bigoplus_{j\in J}N_j$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules] and write $M_B$ for the submodule of vectors supported in $B\subseteq J$ [def-trf-coordinate-submodule]. There is an equality of subsets of $M$, $M_D=\bigcup_{k\in\mathbf N}M_{A_k}$; thus every vector in $M_D$ lies in a single stage coordinate submodule. No generation or countability hypothesis on the modules or on $R$ is imposed.

proof.text: The recursion gives $A_k\subseteq A_{k+1}$, since $A_k$ is the first term in the defining union. Iterating these inclusions gives $A_k\subseteq A_l$ whenever $k\leq l$. Each $A_k$ is contained in $D$ by the definition of $D$, and $C=A_0\subseteq D$.

proof.text: Induct on $k$ to show that $A_k$ is at most countable. The base $A_0=C$ is a hypothesis. If $A_k$ is at most countable, apply the restricted-union clause of [lem-trf-countable-unions] with $X=I=J$, $S=A_k$ and $B_j=F_j$. All $F_j$ are at most countable by hypothesis, so $\bigcup_{j\in A_k}F_j$ is at most countable. Its union with the at most countable set $A_k$ is at most countable by the binary-union clause, giving the induction step.

proof.text: For $j\in D$ there is $k$ with $j\in A_k$. Every element of $F_j$ therefore belongs to $\bigcup_{i\in A_k}F_i\subseteq A_{k+1}\subseteq D$. This proves $F_j\subseteq D$.

source.place: Tag 058X, theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum, proof lines 20511–20552; explicit successor-stage regrouping of the countable support construction.

proof.text: For a finite $E\subseteq D$, prove existence of a containing stage by induction on the number of elements of $E$. The empty subset is contained in $A_0$. For $E=E_0\cup\{j\}$ choose $k$ with $E_0\subseteq A_k$ by induction and $l$ with $j\in A_l$ by membership in $D$. Step 1 gives $A_k,A_l\subseteq A_{\max(k,l)}$, hence $E\subseteq A_{\max(k,l)}$. This includes $E=\varnothing$ without choosing any index from it.

source.place: Tag 058X, theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum, proof lines 20511–20552; explicit successor-stage regrouping of the countable support construction.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], each $x\in M$ has finite support $E=\{j:x_j\ne0\}$. By [def-trf-coordinate-submodule], $x\in M_B$ means precisely $E\subseteq B$. Thus, for $x\in M_D$, step 5 gives $E\subseteq A_k$ for some $k$, and hence $x\in M_{A_k}$. Conversely $x\in M_{A_k}$ implies $E\subseteq A_k\subseteq D$, so $x\in M_D$. These two inclusions prove the claimed equality of subsets of the same ambient $M$. If $x=0$, take $k=0$ since its support is empty. Only finite support was used; $R$ and the $N_j$ need no countability or generation assumption.
